items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Pat would play clarinet and I would play, well during those — when we played the polkas I played piano most of the time.

ctx.x: Did your father write parts for your trumpet playing that — with the fact that you’re seven or eight?

No, no. We just played stock arrangements. We didn’t ease into it. I mean they weren’t that difficult, the stocks weren’t that difficult but we started right out playing stocks. He wrote some polka things out that — he would transcribe some polka parts for the trumpet that were originally for me, and he made the clarinet or mandolin — Pat would play clarinet and I would play, well during those — when we played the polkas I played piano most of the time. But he would copy some parts, yeah, for trumpet, but not a…
For the folks who don’t know, can you explain what stocks means?

items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I got interested in it, I roped my brother John and Joe into it, I got them into it, and then some local kids that were in school with us, I got one of them to play bass and a couple of them played trumpet.

ctx.x: Wow. Was there any rivalry with your brothers regarding music?

No. We’ve always gotten along. We never had any kind of arguments that I can see. Basically I was the first one interested in jazz. I got interested in it, I roped my brother John and Joe into it, I got them into it, and then some local kids that were in school with us, I got one of them to play bass and a couple of them played trumpet. But we never really fought over anything. Even to this day we’re still in kind of an agreement. And it’s kind of unusual. You know I played a club here called The Rex and I know…
